newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ERM-2 norm not to prejudice EMU criteria-Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: ERM-2 norm not to prejudice EMU criteria-Tietmeyer.

text.p: Setting standard 15 percent fluctuation bands in a new Exchange Rate Mechanism to be set up after the launch of economic and monetary union (EMU) would not be prejudicial for EMU currency criteria, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Saturday, after a two-day informal meeting of EU finance ministers.
"There is general agreement that these band widths cannot be identified with the 'normal bands' refered to in the Maastricht Treaty," Tietmeyer said.

The Maastricht Treaty calls for countries which want to join European monetary union to ensure that their currencies have been stable within the 'normal bands' of the European Monetary System for two years before EMU commences.
But it does not define exactly how large the 'normal bands' should be.
Most currencies currently are allowed to fluctuate 15 percent either side of their central rates.

But these wider bands were only created after considerable market turbulence in 1992 and 1993 pushed currency to the limits of the former narrower bands of either 2-1/4 or six percent either side of the central rate.
Some argue that they therefore cannot be considered as 'normal' even though they are the prevailing conditions at the moment.
Tietmeyer declined to comment on how he thought the bands should be defined when it came to the decsion on which currencies were eligible for monetary union.
He said this would be part of the overall decision on which countries qualified for EMU due to take place in early 1998.
